title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 72 (Liability of person to whom money is paid or thing delivered by mistake or coercion)

content.overview: Section 72 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872 requires a person to whom money has been paid, or anything delivered, by mistake or under coercion to repay or return it. The statutory focus is receipt of money or a thing through mistake or coercion; the recipient's obligation is restitution in the form stated by the section. Application to a real dispute requires analysis of the facts and the legal meaning of mistake or coercion.

sections.heading: Statutory rule
sections.body: A person to whom money has been paid, or anything delivered, by mistake or under coercion must repay or return it.

sections.heading: Mistaken duplicate payment
sections.body: The Act illustrates joint debtors where one pays and the other, unaware of the first payment, pays the same sum again. The recipient must repay the duplicate payment.

sections.heading: Payment under coercion
sections.body: The Act illustrates a consignee who pays an illegally excessive carriage charge to obtain goods. The consignee may recover the illegally excessive part of the charge.

sections.heading: Proof and remedy
sections.body: Identify the transfer, recipient, mistake or coercion, causal link and amount or thing to be restored. Preserve payment, delivery and demand records.

examples.title: Duplicate payment of a joint debt
examples.body: A and B jointly owe ₹100 to C. A pays C; B, unaware of that payment, pays C another ₹100. The statutory illustration requires C to repay the duplicate payment to B.

examples.title: Illegally excessive charge
examples.body: A consignee pays an illegally excessive carriage charge to obtain delivery of goods. The statutory illustration supports recovery of the illegally excessive portion, not automatically every charge paid.

hypotheticals.question: A person pays a debt twice because they did not know the first payment had cleared. What issue arises under section 72?
hypotheticals.analysis: The duplicate payment is the kind of situation addressed by the Act's illustration. Establish the first payment, the second payment, the recipient and the amount to be repaid.

hypotheticals.question: A recipient receives goods because of a mistaken delivery. Does section 72 use the same remedy as for money?
hypotheticals.analysis: The text says the recipient must repay money or return anything delivered. The appropriate response depends on the thing delivered and the facts.

hypotheticals.question: A person pays an excessive charge only because delivery was withheld until payment. What must be shown?
hypotheticals.analysis: Identify the demand, the condition imposed, proof of payment, the legal basis for saying the charge was excessive, and the amount claimed back.

content.study:
TEXT OF SECTION 72: “A person to whom money has been paid, or anything delivered, by mistake or under coercion, must repay or return it.”

Core rule: Section 72 imposes a duty to repay money or return a thing received through mistake or coercion. The section is not limited in its wording to a mistake of fact; the meaning and application of mistake, including legal questions raised by a particular dispute, must be assessed against authoritative law rather than assumed from a general summary.

Elements and method:
1. Identify the money paid or thing delivered and the recipient.
2. Determine whether the payment or delivery occurred by mistake or under coercion.
3. Establish the causal connection between the mistake/coercion and the transfer or receipt.
4. Identify the appropriate restitutionary response: repay the money or return the thing, subject to the governing law and facts.
5. Where only part of a payment was excessive or wrongly demanded, quantify the amount for which recovery is claimed and support it with records.

Statutory illustrations: (a) A and B jointly owe ₹100 to C. A pays C, but B, unaware of A's payment, pays C the same ₹100 again. C must repay the duplicate payment to B. (b) A railway company refuses to deliver goods to the consignee unless an illegal carriage charge is paid. The consignee pays to obtain the goods and is entitled to recover the part of the charge that was illegally excessive.

Distinctions: Section 72 concerns restitution of money or things transferred by mistake or under coercion. It should not be treated as identical to section 70's non-gratuitous-benefit rule or section 73's compensation for loss caused by breach. The proper provision depends on the facts and legal basis of the claim.

Evidence checklist: payment/delivery receipts; bank or ledger records; demand or coercion correspondence; delivery/consignment documents; calculation of the duplicate or excessive amount; and the facts showing the mistake or coercion.

Exam structure: quote the rule; identify the transfer and recipient; analyse mistake/coercion; apply the statutory remedy of repayment/return; quantify the claim; distinguish adjacent restitution and damages provisions; conclude on the evidence.

Verification boundary: This is a substantive content pass. Current-law analysis, case-law propositions and final legal verification remain open.

distinctions.explanation: Section 72 addresses repayment or return following a transfer by mistake or coercion; section 70 addresses compensation or restoration for a lawful non-gratuitous act whose benefit is enjoyed.
Section 72's text concerns restitution of money or a thing transferred by mistake or coercion. Section 73 addresses compensation for loss or damage caused by breach of contract.

misconceptions.trap: Section 72 applies only to duplicate payments.
misconceptions.correction: The text covers money paid or anything delivered by mistake or under coercion; duplicate payment is one statutory illustration.

misconceptions.trap: The whole amount of any disputed charge is automatically recoverable.
misconceptions.correction: The statutory illustration refers to the part of a charge that was illegally excessive. Identify and prove the amount claimed.

misconceptions.trap: Section 72 is interchangeable with section 70 or section 73.
misconceptions.correction: Analyse the specific statutory basis: mistake/coercion and repayment/return under s. 72, non-gratuitous benefit under s. 70, or breach-related compensation under s. 73.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the rule under section 72?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: A person who receives money paid, or anything delivered, by mistake or under coercion must repay the money or return the thing.
